name: Newton's prism and the experimentum crucis
scope: How a man in a plague-year bedroom proved white light is a mixture, not a stain. T1: 1665-66, Cambridge closed by plague, Newton at Woolsthorpe bores a hole in his window shutter, catches the sunbeam on a prism -- and the patch on the far wall comes out an OBLONG smear of colours, not the round white spot the reigning theory required. The SHAPE anomaly is what tipped him off. T2: what 'everyone knew' -- colours were a MODIFICATION: white light is pure and simple, and glass stains or weakens it (thicker glass, darker colour). Newton's claim was the opposite: white light is already a MIXTURE, and the prism only sorts what was there. T3 (the payoff rung): the experimentum crucis needed a SECOND prism -- Newton let the first prism spread the spectrum, cut a single colour out through a small hole in a board, and sent that one beam through prism number two. It bent by the same amount and STAYED that colour. It would not split further and it would not change. T3: the reverse test -- Newton reassembled the whole spectrum with a lens and got plain WHITE back out, then blocked one colour and watched the white go off-white. T4: colour belongs to the LIGHT, not the object -- Newton showed a red object under a single pure colour of light looks dark or grey; check it under a sodium street lamp or a single-colour LED, where a red car turns muddy brown. T4: Newton pressed a bodkin (a blunt needle) between his own eyeball and the bone to find out whether the colour was in the light or in his eye -- coloured and dark circles appeared, and he wrote it all down; he also stared at the Sun and had to sit in the dark for days afterward. T4: Newton's own wrong conclusion -- convinced that a lens's colour fringing was incurable, he abandoned refractors and built a REFLECTING telescope in 1668; Chester Moore Hall and John Dollond later cured chromatic aberration with an achromatic doublet Newton had ruled out. T5: the 1672 letter 'New Theory about Light and Colours' to the Royal Society, and Robert Hooke's dismissive reply claiming he'd already done such experiments and they suited his own wave hypothesis -- the fight went so sour that Newton sat on Opticks until 1704, the year after Hooke died. T5: the seven colours are a CHOICE -- Newton saw six bands clearly and inserted 'indigo' to make the count seven, matching the seven notes of a musical scale; the physical spectrum is continuous with no seams. T5: Newton's colour circle in Opticks -- the first colour wheel, built to predict what mixtures would look like, which is a statement about the EYE, not the light. T5: Goethe's 1810 Farbenlehre attacked Newton head-on, insisting colour is born at the boundary between light and dark. Goethe lost on the physics and kept something real: his observations of afterimages and contrast are about perception, which Newton's spectrum does not cover.
source: Grokipedia (Experimentum crucis; Dispersive prism; Opticks; Prism (optics); Early life of Isaac Newton) checked first via site search; corroborated with en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opticks (1672 Royal Society report; Hooke dispute and delayed publication until 1704, Latin 1706; Book I Part II Theorem ii on degree of refrangibility; the colour circle and seven hues); Newton Project (newtonproject.ox.ac.uk) MS 'Of Colours' for the bodkin passage; Wikipedia 'Isaac Newton' and 'Newton's reflector' for the 1668 reflecting telescope and the achromatic-doublet sequel; Wikipedia 'Theory of Colours (Goethe)'.
framing_note: The DISCOVERY flagship of the sub-strand. T1 keys the SHAPE anomaly (an oblong, not a circle), never a date. ACCURACY RAIL: the first-prism spectrum was NOT Newton's discovery -- Descartes, Marci and Grimaldi had all seen prism colours; Newton's novelty is the SECOND prism showing a single colour is primitive and unchangeable, and the term 'experimentum crucis' was Hooke's own from Micrographia (1665), which is the irony worth keeping. Never key 'Newton discovered the spectrum'. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T3 (the isolated beam refuses to change) plus the bodkin. Add a plain do-NOT-repeat line on the bodkin and the sun-staring. DISTRACTOR MINE: the modification hypothesis (glass stains light), Hooke's pulse theory, Descartes' spinning-globule account, Goethe's boundary theory -- all live positions serious people held. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: no stem may say 'white light contains all colours' before asking what Newton proved; describe the room, the shutter, the board with the hole, and let the result be recalled.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank may carry Newton or Goethe as an epistemology case -- this ladder stays on the optical test, not on rationalism vs empiricism. A science MECHANICS/gravity sub-strand owns Newton's laws and the apple anecdote; keep both out of here.

name: Why the sky is blue and the sunset is red
scope: The mechanism you can check every clear evening. T1: the Sun does not change colour at sunset -- YOUR line of sight does. At noon its light crosses a short slab of air; at the horizon it ploughs through many times more atmosphere, and the blue has been scattered out of the beam long before it reaches your eye, leaving orange and red. T2: the blue overhead is not the sky's own colour and there is no blue substance up there -- air MOLECULES, mostly nitrogen and oxygen, redirect short wavelengths far more strongly than long ones, and that redirected blue arrives at your eye from every direction at once. T3: Lord Rayleigh's 1871 law -- scattering strength goes as the inverse FOURTH power of the wavelength, so violet near 400 nm is scattered roughly ten times harder than red near 700 nm. Small change in wavelength, huge change in effect. T3: then why isn't the sky VIOLET? Two honest reasons, and neither is 'violet scatters less': sunlight simply contains less violet, and human cones are far less sensitive to violet than to blue. The sky's colour is set partly by your own retina. T4: John Tyndall got there first with apparatus, not algebra -- in 1869 he made a blue sky in a glass tube by scattering a beam through a fine mist, and found the scattered light was both blue AND polarized. The theory he inspired then killed his own assumption: Rayleigh showed molecules alone suffice, so DUST is not required and 'the sky is blue because of dust' is wrong. T4: clouds are white made of the same water and the same sunlight -- their droplets are LARGE compared with a wavelength, which puts them in a different regime (Mie scattering) that treats all colours nearly equally. Size, not substance. T4: the ocean is blue for a COMPLETELY different reason, and 'it reflects the sky' is wrong -- water itself absorbs red light through overtone vibrations of its O-H bonds, the one common colour in nature produced by molecular vibration rather than by electrons. Check it in deep glacier ice or a long white-bottomed pool, where the blue survives on an overcast day. T5: Einstein's 1910 refinement -- a perfectly uniform gas would not scatter at all; scattering comes from random DENSITY FLUCTUATIONS as molecules jostle, and the same mathematics let him extract an estimate of Avogadro's number from the colour of the sky. T5: the sky's light is polarized in a great band about 90 degrees from the Sun, which is why a polarizing filter darkens one part of a photographed sky and not another. T3: distant mountains fade to hazy blue by the same scattering over a horizontal path -- Leonardo da Vinci noticed it, named it aerial perspective and painted with it centuries before anyone could explain it.
source: Grokipedia (Rayleigh scattering; Sky blue; Tyndall effect; Diffuse sky radiation; Atmospheric optics; Rayleigh sky model) checked first via site search -- Tyndall 1869 colloid experiments, Rayleigh 1871 theory, 1/lambda^4, Einstein 1910 density-fluctuation derivation; corroborated with Braun & Smirnov, 'Why Is Water Blue?', J. Chem. Educ. 70(8) 612 (1993) via webexhibits.org full text and NMSU mirror for water's vibrational-overtone absorption; Wikipedia 'Diffuse sky radiation' and 'Mie scattering' for the cloud/droplet size regime.
framing_note: The MECHANISM flagship and the strongest test-it-yourself ladder here -- frame every rung as an invitation (look at the sunset, look at a cloud, look into deep water). ACCURACY RAIL 1: it is not 'blue scatters, red doesn't' but a smooth 1/lambda^4 gradient, and the sky is not violet because of the solar spectrum plus cone sensitivity -- never let a rung imply violet scatters less. ACCURACY RAIL 2: the ocean's blue is intrinsic absorption by water, NOT reflected sky -- that correction is a rung, so no other rung may casually say the sea mirrors the sky. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: the sunset rung (T1) and the ocean correction (T4). DISTRACTOR MINE: dust or pollution causes the blue (Tyndall's own first framing), the sea reflecting into the sky, ozone tinting the air, 'the atmosphere is blue-tinted glass', and Mie scattering offered where Rayleigh belongs. LANE: GEOGRAPHY tours places and weather; this ladder owns the scattering LAW and its discoverers and must never become a place-tour.
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY bank may cover volcanic or desert sunsets place-first (e.g. Krakatoa skies) -- key every rung here to the LAW and the named discoverers, not to a place. A science EARTH/ATMOSPHERE sub-strand owns the composition of air and the greenhouse effect -- reference air's nitrogen/oxygen in one clause only.

name: The rainbow you can build with a garden hose
scope: Geometry you can walk into on any sunny afternoon. T1: stand with your back to a low Sun and spray a hose in front of you -- the bow appears centred exactly on the shadow of your own HEAD (the antisolar point). Every rainbow anyone has ever seen is aimed personally at the viewer. T2: the 42-degree rule -- every drop that sends red light to your eye lies on a cone about 42 degrees wide around that antisolar line, with violet near 40 degrees. That fixed angle is why every rainbow in history is the same size, and why the bow is a DIRECTION rather than an object sitting at a place. T3: inside a single drop, light refracts on entry, bounces ONCE off the back, refracts on the way out; the rays pile up at a minimum bend of about 138 degrees, and that pile-up is what makes a bright arc instead of a smear. Descartes worked it out in 1637 by tracing thousands of rays by hand. T3: you can never reach the end of a rainbow, and two people standing side by side are seeing bows built from DIFFERENT drops -- step sideways and the bow is remade from new water. T4: the fainter SECONDARY bow sits near 51 degrees with its colours REVERSED, red on the inside, because light bounces twice inside the drop; and the sky between the two bows is genuinely darker -- Alexander's band, named for Alexander of Aphrodisias, who noticed the gap around AD 200. Look for the reversed order tonight. T4: Theodoric of Freiberg tested it around 1307 with a glass globe of water as one gigantic raindrop, tracing the one-bounce and two-bounce paths -- and Kamal al-Din al-Farisi reached the same result independently in Persia within about two years. T4: what Descartes could NOT do was explain the colours; Newton supplied that piece -- the drop is a prism, and dispersion spreads the bend angle by roughly two degrees, which is exactly the width of the coloured band. T5: the faint pastel fringes sometimes crowded just inside the primary bow -- supernumerary bows -- cannot be produced by ray tracing at all. They are interference between rays that took slightly different paths through the drop, explained by George Airy in 1838, and their spacing reports the DROP SIZE. T5: from an aeroplane a rainbow closes into a full CIRCLE because drops below your horizon are now in play; and on a bright night a moonbow appears, too dim for your colour vision but plainly coloured in a long camera exposure. T3: the bands are blurry because the Sun is about half a degree wide -- a true point-source sun would throw a razor-sharp spectrum.
source: Grokipedia (Rainbow; Alexander's band) checked first via site search -- 42-degree angular radius, antisolar point, secondary at ~51 degrees with reversed colours, the 138-degree and 231-degree minimum deviations; corroborated with en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow (42.5 degrees red vs ~40 degrees violet, secondary 50-53 degrees, full-circle bows from aircraft, supernumerary bands as interference, historical sequence Theodoric of Freiberg 1307 / Kamal al-Din al-Farisi 1309 / Descartes 1637 / Newton); arXiv 1811.12053 'Descartes-Newton-Young rainbow' and arXiv 2603.15629 'Rainbow formation: from Descartes to Venus' for the deviation-minimum and Airy-theory framing.
framing_note: The TEST-IT-YOURSELF flagship -- every rung must be checkable with a hose, a sprinkler, a lawn on a wet morning, or a glass of water. ACCURACY RAIL: red sits at about 42 degrees and violet near 40 -- do not copy Wikipedia's garbled '350 nm' figure for violet; and the bow is not located AT the rain, it is an angle, so no stem may place the rainbow 'over there by the trees'. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T1 (it is centred on your own shadow) and the reversed secondary. DISTRACTOR MINE: the bow is sunlight reflecting off the cloud face, the drops act as tiny mirrors, water is faintly tinted, the bow hangs at a fixed place in the sky, and the plausible-but-wrong 'the secondary is just a reflection of the primary'. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never say 'one internal reflection' in a stem that asks why the secondary's colours are reversed. Keep pot-of-gold folklore entirely out -- that belongs to trivia/theology, not here.

name: Clocking light: Jupiter's moons to a mountain top
scope: A CONCEPT ladder across the measurement chain -- how a speed nobody could feel got pinned down. T1: 1676, Paris Observatory -- Ole Romer notices the eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io run EARLY when Earth is near Jupiter and LATE when Earth is far, announces on 21 November that the coming eclipse will arrive about ten minutes behind the printed tables, and it does. He used a moon as a clock. T2: the number Romer actually gave was not a speed -- he said light takes about 22 minutes to cross the DIAMETER of Earth's orbit (the modern figure is about 16.7 minutes); Christiaan Huygens turned that into a distance-per-second in 1678, and Romer never published a full account of his own. T3: his own boss fought him -- Giovanni Cassini objected that the other Galilean moons did not show the effect as crisply and preferred to patch the tables empirically; acceptance took roughly half a century. T3: the settlement arrived from a different puzzle -- James Bradley found in 1728 that every star traces a tiny annual ellipse, because you must tilt the telescope forward while Earth moves, the way you tilt an umbrella when you run. From that tilt he got 8 minutes 12 seconds for sunlight to reach Earth; the modern value is 8 minutes 19 seconds. T2: Galileo had already tried, and said so honestly -- in Two New Sciences (1638) he describes two men with shuttered lanterns on hilltops about a mile apart, and reports he could detect no delay, concluding only that light is 'if not instantaneous, extraordinarily rapid'. Light crosses a mile in about five millionths of a second; human reaction time is tens of thousands of times too slow. T3: the first measurement made entirely on the ground -- Hippolyte Fizeau, 1849, sends a beam 8.633 km from Suresnes to a mirror on Montmartre and back through the gaps of a wheel carrying 720 teeth; spin the wheel fast enough and the returning flash is blocked by the NEXT tooth. Result: 313,300 km/s, about 4 percent high. T4 (payoff): Leon Foucault swapped the wheel for a spinning MIRROR, needed only about 20 metres of bench -- and then settled a 150-year-old argument by measuring light in WATER. It goes SLOWER there. Newton's particle theory required it to go FASTER. One measurement, one dead theory. T4: Albert Michelson's lifelong obsession -- an improvised rig as a young naval instructor in 1878, then 1879 at Annapolis (299,864 km/s), then in 1926 a beam fired between Mount Wilson and a peak about 35 km away off an octagonal rotating mirror, with the baseline surveyed by the US Coast and Geodetic Survey: 299,796 +/- 4 km/s. He died in 1931 mid-experiment; his final value was published posthumously in 1935. T5: measuring c stopped in 1983 -- the metre was REDEFINED as the distance light travels in 1/299,792,458 of a second, so the speed of light is now exact by definition and every later 'measurement of c' is really a measurement of the metre. T5 (MYSTERY): nobody has ever measured the ONE-WAY speed of light. Every experiment times a round trip, because the two clocks at each end must first be synchronised -- and any way of synchronising them already assumes the answer. This is a real, open, honestly-stated loophole, not a crank claim. T5: the 1887 Michelson-Morley result -- an interferometer built to catch Earth's motion through the luminiferous ether found nothing at all, the most productive failed experiment in physics, and the ether joined phlogiston and caloric in the graveyard.
source: Grokipedia (Ole Romer; Romer's determination of the speed of light; Hippolyte Fizeau; Fizeau's measurement of the speed of light in air; Foucault's measurements of the speed of light; Albert A. Michelson; Speed of light; Aberration (astronomy); One-way speed of light) checked first via site search; corroborated with en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%B8mer%27s_determination_of_the_speed_of_light (21 Nov 1676 announcement, the ~10-minute prediction, the 22-minute orbital-diameter figure, Romer publishing no formal description, Huygens' 110,000,000 toises/s, Cassini's opposition, Bradley 1729 giving 8 min 13 s) and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_A._Michelson (1878 improvised work, 1879 Annapolis 299,864 +/- 51 km/s, 1887 Michelson-Morley null result, 1907 Nobel, 1926 Mount Wilson 299,796 +/- 4 km/s, posthumous 1935 value 299,774 +/- 11 km/s); Springer 'Galileo's Work on Sound and Speed of Light' (10.1007/978-3-030-51744-1_29) and NHN/OU 'History of the Speed of Light' for the 1638 lantern trial and Galileo's own conclusion.
framing_note: The analytic BACKBONE of this sub-strand -- a theme ladder that carries the T4/T5 ceiling by running one method across named cases. ACCURACY RAIL 1: Romer gave a TIME (about 22 minutes across Earth's orbit), never a km/s figure -- do not key '227,000 km/s' as Romer's own result; that back-calculation is later. RAIL 2: 'the Academy rejected him for fifty years' is embroidered -- Cassini personally opposed it (having himself floated finite speed in 1675 and dropped it); say 'opposed', not 'voted down'. RAIL 3: sources disagree on the far end of Michelson's 1926 baseline (Lookout Mountain / Mount San Antonio) -- write the DISTANCE (~35 km, 22 miles) and settle the peak name at build time or omit it. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: Foucault's water measurement killing the particle theory, and the one-way loophole. DISTRACTOR MINE: the luminiferous ether, instantaneous propagation (Descartes' committed position -- he bet on it and lost), Newton's corpuscles predicting light speeds UP in water, and Galileo's inconclusive lanterns offered as a success. Keep every rung to arithmetic a grade-10 student can follow; no Lorentz transformations.
history_overlap: A science RELATIVITY/modern-physics sub-strand almost certainly owns Michelson-Morley's consequences -- this ladder keys the ETHER's death and the measurement chain only, never the relativity postulates, time dilation or length contraction. GEOGRAPHY/HISTORY may carry Jupiter's moons as an 18th-century longitude method for mapmaking -- keep any such rung out of this ladder.

name: Fraunhofer's dark lines and the philosopher's impossible
scope: How a barcode in sunlight answered a question a great thinker declared unanswerable forever. T1: orphaned at 11 and apprenticed to a harsh Munich mirror-polisher who denied him books and candlelight, 14-year-old Joseph Fraunhofer was buried under rubble on 21 July 1801 when the workshop roof collapsed -- others died; he was dug out, in view of the Elector of Bavaria, who gave him money and a way out. The accident made the career. T2: 1814 -- Fraunhofer, testing his own world-class glass, builds a prism-and-telescope spectroscope, points it at the Sun and finds the spectrum is not a smooth rainbow at all: it is cut by hundreds of sharp DARK lines. He maps about 574 of them, labels the strongest A through K, and states plainly that he cannot explain them. T3: the coincidence nobody could shake -- the double dark line Fraunhofer had labelled D fell at precisely the wavelength where a sodium flame in a laboratory makes a BRIGHT yellow line. Same place, opposite colour. T3: Heidelberg, 1859-60 -- Robert Bunsen's nearly colourless gas flame finally let a chemist burn a sample without the flame's own light drowning the result, and Gustav Kirchhoff found each element gives its own fixed set of bright lines. An unforgeable barcode per element. T4 (mechanism): Kirchhoff's inversion -- send white light through a COOLER gas and the same lines come back DARK: a gas absorbs exactly the wavelengths it emits. So the Sun's dark lines are a list of what sits in the Sun's cooler outer layers, readable from a bench in Germany. T4: within two years the method found elements nobody had ever seen -- caesium, named for a sky-blue line, and rubidium, named for a deep red one, both discovered by spectrum before anyone isolated them. The barcode reads unknowns, not just knowns. T5 (payoff, REVERSAL): in 1835, in the 19th lesson of his Cours de philosophie positive, Auguste Comte wrote that we could learn the stars' shapes, distances, sizes and motions but 'would never know how to study by any means their chemical composition'. Within roughly 25 years astronomers were reading the Sun's composition off a wall. The philosopher's permanent impossible became a school laboratory exercise. T4: told that Kirchhoff had detected gold in the Sun, his banker asked what earthly use that was if you could not fetch it; when Kirchhoff's Rumford Medal prize arrived from London in gold sovereigns he handed them over with the line that here, at last, was gold from the Sun. T5: the same lines carry MOTION -- William Huggins measured Sirius's lines shifted slightly toward the red in 1868 and got a speed along the line of sight; the trick later gave Hubble an expanding universe and today finds planets by the wobble they impose on their star. T4: the honest limit -- a spectrum gives composition and line-of-sight motion, but not distance or age, and lines shift and broaden with pressure, temperature and magnetic field. Reading a spectrum is a chain of inference, not a photograph. T3: Fraunhofer died at 39 of tuberculosis, likely worsened by years of heavy-metal fumes from his glass furnaces; his epitaph reads Approximavit sidera -- he brought the stars nearer. T2: check it yourself -- tilt a CD or DVD under a compact fluorescent or LED bulb and you get a spectrum with obvious BRIGHT lines and gaps, visibly different from the smooth sunlit spectrum on the same disc.
source: Grokipedia (Joseph von Fraunhofer; Fraunhofer lines; History of spectroscopy; Spectroscopy; Atomic spectroscopy) checked first via site search -- the 1798 orphaning, the 1799 apprenticeship to Philipp Anton Weichselberger, the 21 July 1801 workshop collapse, the 1814 spectroscope, ~574 lines labelled A-K, Kirchhoff and Bunsen 1859 linking dark and bright lines; corroborated with en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_Kirchhoff (the three laws of spectroscopy, sodium in the Sun 1859, caesium and rubidium, 1862 Rumford Medal, the banker/gold anecdote); Comte quotation via libquotes.com and unm.edu/~soc101/quoteauguste.htm (Cours de philosophie positive, 19th lesson, 1835) plus Cambridge University Press 'Analysis of Starlight' introduction for the ~25-year refutation framing; Wikipedia 'William Huggins' for the 1868 Sirius radial-velocity measurement.
framing_note: The REVERSAL flagship: an eminent thinker declared a question permanently closed and the answer arrived within a generation -- and the bank lets that land WITHOUT editorialising about experts. ACCURACY RAIL 1: quote Comte correctly. He did not write 'we will never know what the stars are made of'; he wrote that we may determine stars' forms, distances, sizes and motions but never their chemical composition or mineralogical structure. Key the CLAIM and its source, never a fabricated sentence. RAIL 2: William Hyde Wollaston saw a handful of dark lines in 1802 and read them as gaps between colours -- Fraunhofer's contribution is the systematic MAP, not first sight; never key 'Fraunhofer was the first to see a dark line'. RAIL 3: nail the caesium/rubidium years at build time (commonly 1860 and 1861 respectively; one source here says both 1861). RAIL 4: the banker story is a well-attested anecdote (via Roscoe) -- present it as an anecdote, not as minuted fact. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: the Comte rung, then the banker. DISTRACTOR MINE: the lines are gaps in the Sun's own light (Wollaston's reading), flaws in the prism glass, and the genuinely half-true one -- some Fraunhofer bands (A and B) really ARE caused by oxygen in EARTH's atmosphere, so build that carefully as an adjacent-but-not-the-keyed-answer option, never as a trap that is secretly correct.
history_overlap: PHILOSOPHY bank owns Comte as the founder of positivism -- this ladder keys only his stars claim and its empirical refutation, never positivism as a doctrine. The helium ladder in this same sub-strand owns the 1868 eclipse yellow line -- do not duplicate it here. A science CHEMISTRY/periodic-table sub-strand may own caesium and rubidium as alkali metals -- key them here purely as spectroscopy's first new elements.

name: Helium: found in the Sun before it was found on Earth
scope: The one element humanity met in the sky first. T2: 18 August 1868, total eclipse, Guntur, India -- Pierre Janssen turns a spectroscope on a solar prominence and records a bright yellow line at 587.6 nm sitting close beside, but plainly not on, the familiar sodium lines. A colour no known substance on Earth could make. T2: Janssen's second result mattered as much -- the prominence lines were so bright he realised he could see them in ordinary DAYLIGHT without waiting for an eclipse; Norman Lockyer hit on the same daylight method in London within weeks, and the French Academy struck a single medal carrying both their faces. T3: Lockyer and the chemist Edward Frankland named the unknown HELIUM after helios, the Sun -- naming an element nobody had ever held struck many chemists as reckless, and for nearly thirty years helium was a line on a chart and nothing else. T4: 26 March 1895 -- William Ramsay treats the uranium mineral cleveite with acid, collects the gas that comes off, and the spectroscope shows the same yellow line. The Sun's element had been sitting in a rock in a drawer; Per Teodor Cleve and Nils Langlet reached it independently in Sweden the same year. T4: the honest priority caveat -- Luigi Palmieri reported the same yellow line in Vesuvius lava in 1881, but the work could not be reproduced and does not count as isolation. T5 (the method's own failures): the same spectroscopic logic also produced two elements that do not exist -- 'coronium', invented for an unexplained green line in the solar corona, and 'nebulium', invented for lines in glowing nebulae. Both were phantoms: Ira Bowen showed in 1927 that nebulium was doubly-ionised OXYGEN, and Grotrian and Edlen showed around 1939-41 that coronium was iron stripped of thirteen electrons at millions of degrees. Helium was real; the other two were the method overreaching. T5: helium is the second most abundant element in the UNIVERSE and genuinely scarce on Earth, and the reason is physics -- it is light enough to escape our gravity, so essentially all the helium we use is radiogenic, alpha particles from uranium and thorium decay trapped underground in natural gas. Vent a balloon and that helium leaves the planet permanently. T5: helium's stubborn refusal to liquefy paid off -- Heike Kamerlingh Onnes finally condensed it in 1908 at 4.2 kelvin, and three years later, using it, discovered superconductivity in mercury; and below 2.17 K liquid helium becomes a superfluid that creeps up and over the walls of its own container.
source: Grokipedia (Helium; Helium-4; PJC Janssen; Norman Lockyer; Cosmochemistry; History of the periodic table) checked first via site search -- 18 Aug 1868 Guntur eclipse, the 587.6 nm line, Lockyer's daylight confirmation and the helios naming with Frankland, Ramsay's 26 March 1895 isolation from cleveite; corroborated with Wikipedia 'Helium' (Palmieri's 1881 Vesuvius claim, Cleve and Langlet's independent Swedish isolation, radiogenic terrestrial origin and escape), Wikipedia 'Nebulium' (Bowen 1927, doubly-ionised oxygen) and 'Coronium' (Grotrian and Edlen, highly ionised iron), Wikipedia 'Heike Kamerlingh Onnes' (helium liquefied 1908, superconductivity 1911) and 'Superfluid helium-4' (lambda point 2.17 K).
framing_note: DISCOVERY plus a genuine wonder hook -- we read an element off the sky before we ever touched it. ACCURACY RAIL 1: do not key a single 'discoverer of helium'. Janssen made the eclipse observation (18 Aug 1868), Lockyer made the daylight observation and, with Frankland, the naming -- both claims are real and the medal honoured both. RAIL 2: Earth's helium is radiogenic alpha decay trapped in gas fields, not primordial leftovers -- state the scarcity mechanism correctly. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T2 (a colour no earthly substance made) and the coronium/nebulium rung, which is the honesty beat -- the same brilliant method also produced two elements that were never there. DISTRACTOR MINE: sodium (the D lines it sits beside), hydrogen, coronium and nebulium themselves (real proposed elements, now the perfect adjacent-but-wrong options), and the wrong-mechanism claim that Earth's helium is left over from the planet's formation. Do NOT re-teach absorption vs emission here -- that is the Fraunhofer ladder's job; this ladder USES it.
history_overlap: The Fraunhofer/Kirchhoff ladder in this sub-strand owns the barcode mechanism and Kirchhoff's inversion -- reference, never re-teach. A science CHEMISTRY sub-strand may own helium as a noble gas and Kamerlingh Onnes as cryogenics/superconductivity -- keep the T5 cryogenic rung to a single consequence clause so a chemistry ladder can own the physics of superconductivity.

name: Herschel's thermometer past the red
scope: The kid-replicable discovery of light you cannot see. T1: 1800, Slough -- William Herschel slides a blackened-bulb thermometer along a prism's spectrum, reading the temperature colour by colour, and then moves it just PAST the red edge into the region where there is nothing at all to see. The reading climbs HIGHER than in any visible colour. The hottest spot was where there was no light. T2: why he was doing it in the first place -- Herschel observed the Sun through coloured filters and had noticed that different colours of glass let through wildly different amounts of HEAT, some of them painfully so. He was chasing a practical safety problem, not a theory. T3: he had already built in the guard against fooling himself -- control thermometers sat outside the beam, so a room warming up on its own could not be mistaken for a result. That control is the whole reason the discovery stands. T3: he named them 'calorific rays' and argued they obey the SAME laws as visible light, showing they reflect and refract like it -- against the live rival view that heat was a separate substance (caloric) merely travelling alongside. Herschel had it right, and the word 'infrared' would not exist for decades. T3 (invitation): you can repeat it this weekend -- a glass prism, a sunny window and three cheap thermometers with blackened bulbs; the space past red reads warmest. And with no equipment at all: point a phone camera at a TV remote and press a button, because most phone sensors see the infrared LED your eyes cannot. T4: the honest caveat modern physicists insist on -- a GLASS prism does not spread wavelengths evenly, so the exact position where Herschel's heat peaked is partly an artefact of his prism. The existence of invisible radiation beyond red is not an artefact; the peak location is. T4: what infrared became -- every warm object glows in it, which is why thermal cameras find people in smoke, why the James Webb Space Telescope is an infrared instrument chilled to around 40 kelvin, and why John Tyndall's 1859 bench measurements of infrared absorption by water vapour and carbon dioxide matter to Earth's temperature. T5: the pattern worth naming -- Herschel had already found Uranus in 1781 with a telescope whose mirrors he ground himself, and he found infrared while solving a practical annoyance. Instrument-builders find things that theorists were not looking for.

ACCURACY RAIL: the invisible radiation past red is real; the POSITION of Herschel's heat maximum is partly a prism artefact -- say both, and never let a rung imply Herschel knew about an electromagnetic spectrum (that is Maxwell, sixty years later) or that he had a wave/frequency picture. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: the phone-camera-sees-the-TV-remote rung. DISTRACTOR MINE: caloric (heat as a weightless fluid -- the reigning rival, and Herschel's actual opponent), phlogiston, 'the prism glass was simply warm', and the tidy-sounding wrong answer that red light is the hot colour. LANE: an EARTH/CLIMATE sub-strand owns Tyndall's greenhouse work -- name it here in one clause and build no climate rung.

name: Ritter's ultraviolet: the other invisible end
scope: The mirror-image discovery, made with chemistry instead of heat. T2: within a year of Herschel, Johann Wilhelm Ritter reasoned that if the spectrum runs on invisibly past red it should run on past VIOLET too -- but there was no heat to feel at that end, so on 22 February 1801 he used a CHEMICAL detector instead: paper soaked in silver chloride, which darkens in light. Beyond the violet edge, where his eyes saw nothing, the paper darkened FASTEST of all. He detected light with a chemical reaction. T3: he called them 'chemical rays' (also deoxidising rays); 'ultraviolet' and 'infrared' were coined decades later. And the darkening he used was the same reaction photography would be built on -- Carl Wilhelm Scheele had described silver chloride blackening in 1777, and within forty years it gave Daguerre and Talbot their pictures. T3: the honest note on his motive -- Ritter belonged to the German Romantic Naturphilosophie circle and was hunting for POLARITY, an opposite to Herschel's heat rays, on essentially metaphysical grounds. The hunch pointed him at something real; the hunch was still not evidence, and plenty of his other work led nowhere. T4: the cost of testing on yourself -- Ritter ran voltaic piles on his own eyes, tongue and nose, recorded the sensations in detail, wrecked his health and died at 33 in 1810, in debt. Barry Marshall drank his beaker and won a Nobel; Ritter is the same courage with the other ending. T4: what UV actually DOES and why it matters -- an ultraviolet photon carries enough energy to break chemical bonds, which is why it burns skin and fades curtains while a much hotter red heat lamp does not. Window glass blocks most UVB, which is why you do not tan through a closed car window -- but UVA does get through, documented in the 2012 New England Journal of Medicine photograph of a delivery driver whose left cheek had aged decades ahead of his right after 28 years at the wheel. T5: UV beads that stay white indoors and turn colour outdoors make the invisible visible in ten seconds, and photographing flowers in UV reveals bullseye 'nectar guides' printed on petals that no human eye has ever seen unaided.
source: Grokipedia (Johann Wilhelm Ritter; Ultraviolet; Ultraviolet photography; Actinism; Blacklight) checked first via site search -- the 22 February 1801 silver-chloride experiment, maximum blackening beyond violet, the 'chemical rays' naming; corroborated with Wikipedia 'Johann Wilhelm Ritter' (Naturphilosophie context, self-experimentation with voltaic piles, death in 1810 aged 33) and Wikipedia 'Silver chloride'/'History of photography' (Scheele 1777); Gordon & Brieva, 'Unilateral Dermatoheliosis', New England Journal of Medicine 366:e25 (2012) for the truck-driver photograph.
framing_note: The companion to Herschel, and the sub-strand's honest counterweight on self-experimentation -- Marshall's beaker made him famous; Ritter's piles killed him at 33. Say both. ACCURACY RAIL 1: Ritter detected UV chemically, not by heat -- never let a rung imply he used a thermometer; the whole point is that he needed a different detector because UV carries little heat. RAIL 2: the truck-driver photograph is a real 2012 NEJM case report by Jennifer Gordon and Joaquin Brieva -- cite it or drop the rung; no unsourced 'a study showed'. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: the UV-beads / no-tan-through-glass rung, both checkable in a day. DISTRACTOR MINE: a thermometer as the detector (Herschel's method, adjacent and wrong here), caloric, phosphorescence, and the plausible-sounding error that UV burns because it is hotter rather than because each photon carries more energy. TEACH-BEFORE-TEST: define 'photon energy per particle of light' in plain words before any rung leans on it.
history_overlap: ANIMAL bank owns bee and bird ultraviolet VISION as a creature adaptation -- key the nectar-guide rung to the UV PHOTOGRAPH that reveals the pattern, not to the animal's eye. A science CHEMISTRY sub-strand may own silver-halide photography -- reference in one clause only.

name: The bright spot that was meant to kill the wave theory
scope: A prediction designed as a refutation that turned into the proof. T2: 1818 -- the French Academy of Sciences sets a prize competition on diffraction, widely expected to vindicate Newton's particle theory of light; an obscure road engineer, Augustin-Jean Fresnel, submits a memoir built entirely on waves. T3 (payoff): the judge Simeon Denis Poisson, a committed particle man, works through Fresnel's own mathematics and derives a consequence he considers self-evidently absurd -- if waves are right, the shadow of a small ROUND disc must have a BRIGHT SPOT dead in the centre. He presents it to sink the theory. T3: Francois Arago, chairing the committee, simply goes and looks -- he mounts a small disc, lights it, and finds the spot exactly where Poisson said it could not be. Fresnel wins the prize; the spot has carried Poisson's name ever since. T3 (mechanism): the spot exists because the obstacle is perfectly ROUND -- every point on the wave grazing the rim is the same distance from the shadow's centre, so all those contributions arrive in step and add up. It is checkable at home with a ball bearing glued to glass and a laser pointer. T4 (epistemic rung): the honest footnote -- the spot had already been SEEN and published by Joseph-Nicolas Delisle in 1715 and Giacomo Maraldi in 1723, and then forgotten. An observation can sit in the literature for a century and count for nothing until a theory makes it matter. T2: the wave case had been opened earlier by Thomas Young, who around 1801-1803 at the Royal Institution split a sunbeam with a thin card and with closely spaced apertures and got alternating BANDS of light and dark. Two beams of light making DARKNESS where they overlap is something particles cannot do. T3: Young was savaged for it -- anonymous attacks in the Edinburgh Review, written by Henry Brougham, were vicious enough that a publisher dropped his lectures and Young redirected his energies to medicine and, later, to Egyptian hieroglyphs. National loyalty to Newton was part of the hostility. T4: Fresnel's success forced something everyone found repellent -- polarization required light to be a TRANSVERSE wave wobbling sideways, which in turn required the ether to behave like a rigid solid filling all space. The picture was absurd, the predictions were right, and the ether died seventy years later anyway. A correct theory can ride on a wrong mental image. T5: Fresnel's monument is practical -- the stepped Fresnel lens of 1822 let a lighthouse throw a usable beam more than 30 km with a fraction of the glass and weight, and the same design sits in overhead projectors and car headlamps today. T5 (invitation): hold two fingers almost touching, a hand's width from your eye, against a bright sky -- the dark bands you see in the gap are diffraction, no equipment at all. A laser pointer shone through a slit cut in foil, or past a single hair, throws the fringe pattern onto a wall. T5: the honest sequel -- waves won so completely that light was considered settled for eighty years, until the photoelectric effect in 1905 forced particles back into the story. Neither picture alone is the whole truth, and the argument reopened.
source: Grokipedia (Arago spot; Augustin-Jean Fresnel; Simeon Denis Poisson; Francois Arago; Fresnel zone; Young's interference experiment) checked first via site search -- the 1818 Academy competition, Poisson's reductio, Arago's 1819 confirmation with a small disc; corroborated with en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young%27s_interference_experiment (Bakerian lectures 1800/1801/1803, the paper-card beam splitting and the ripple tank, ambiguity over whether the classic double slit was actually performed, and Henry Brougham's anonymous Edinburgh Review attacks of 1803-04); Wikipedia 'Arago spot' for the prior observations by Delisle (1715) and Maraldi (1723); Wikipedia 'Fresnel lens' for the 1822 lighthouse lens.
framing_note: The flagship of 'a real test can destroy the person who designed it' -- the sub-strand's cleanest picture of what a good experiment looks like in practice. ACCURACY RAIL 1: Poisson intended the bright spot as a REDUCTIO AD ABSURDUM against Fresnel -- say that plainly; a stem that presents him as predicting a discovery guts the story. RAIL 2: Young's actual demonstrations, as documented, were a beam split by a thin card and a water-ripple tank; the pristine textbook double slit is partly retrospective tidying -- do not key 'Young performed the double-slit experiment' as flat fact. RAIL 3: Arago's test is 1819; the prize memoir is 1818. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T3, Poisson's own arithmetic wrecking Poisson's own theory. DISTRACTOR MINE: Newton's corpuscles (the reigning view), the luminiferous ether, Grimaldi's 1665 diffraction (real, and he read it as light being a fluid), and 'the light bent around the edge because air refracted it'. LANE: PHILOSOPHY owns Popper and falsification as doctrine -- no Popper vocabulary here; this ladder shows the practice and lets the kid see it.
history_overlap: A science QUANTUM/modern-physics sub-strand owns the one-photon-at-a-time double slit and wave-particle duality -- this ladder stops at the classical wave victory and only flags in one T5 clause that the question reopened in 1905. PHILOSOPHY bank owns falsification as doctrine.

name: Polarization: the hidden direction in light
scope: A property of light nobody suspected, discovered by a man staring out of a window. T2: 1808, Paris -- Etienne-Louis Malus looks at the setting Sun reflected in the windows of the Luxembourg Palace through a crystal of Iceland spar, which normally shows everything DOUBLED. As he turns the crystal, one of the two images winks out completely. Plain reflection off glass had done something to the light that no theory expected. T3 (mechanism, teach the term first): light's wave wobbles sideways, and reflection off a flat surface picks out one wobble direction over the other. That is exactly why polarized sunglasses erase the glare off water and a wet road but do very little for the glare off a chrome bumper -- the trick works on horizontal NON-metallic surfaces near a particular angle, not on metal. T3: Edwin Land made it cheap while still a Harvard undergraduate -- in 1929 he aligned microscopic herapathite crystals in plastic (J-sheet), then in 1938 replaced them with stretched, iodine-doped polyvinyl alcohol (H-sheet), which is what sits in your sunglasses and in the front of every LCD screen made since. T4: the SKY is polarized -- light scattered about 90 degrees from the Sun comes out strongly polarized in a great band across the sky, which is why a polarizing filter deepens the blue in one part of a photograph and not another. Put on polarized sunglasses, face 90 degrees from the Sun and tilt your head. T4 (best invitation in the sub-strand): you can see polarization with your NAKED EYE. Stare at a bright, evenly polarized field -- a white LCD screen, or that patch of blue sky -- and a faint yellow bowtie shimmer appears at the centre of your vision and rotates when you tilt your head. It is called Haidinger's brush, it fades in seconds through neural adaptation, and most people go a whole life without being told to look for it. T4: honeybees fly a straight course by that sky pattern when the Sun itself is behind cloud -- Karl von Frisch established it experimentally and shared the 1973 Nobel Prize with Lorenz and Tinbergen. T5 (MYSTERY): the Viking 'sunstone'. Icelandic sagas mention a solarsteinn used to find the Sun in fog, calcite would physically work, and planetarium tests show navigators could locate a hidden Sun with one. But the only crystal actually recovered with navigation instruments came from a 1592 ELIZABETHAN wreck off Alderney, five centuries after the Viking age, and no sunstone has ever been found in a Viking ship or grave. Plausible, testable, and still unproven -- the bank says so. T5: your screen is two crossed polarizers with a twistable liquid crystal sandwiched between them; voltage untwists the crystal and the pixel goes dark. Which is why an LCD screen can black out entirely when you tilt your polarized sunglasses, and why some car dashboards vanish while you are wearing them. T5: squeeze or bend clear plastic between two polarizing filters and rainbow stress contours blaze out of it -- photoelasticity, which engineers used to hunt stress concentrations in models of bridges and dams before computers could calculate them. Two pairs of polarized sunglasses and a plastic fork will show it.

Land; Brewster's angle; Linear polarization; Sunstone (medieval); Karl von Frisch) checked first via site search -- the 1808 Luxembourg Palace observation and the vanishing second image, Land's 1929 J-sheet and 1938 H-sheet, the Alderney 1592 wreck calcite, von Frisch on skylight polarization and the 1973 Nobel; corroborated with en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polarizer (Brewster's angle, s-polarized reflection from horizontal dielectric surfaces, H-sheet PVA/iodine construction) and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haidinger%27s_brush plus polarization.com/haidinger for the naked-eye bowtie, its yellow/blue geometry, the 90-degrees-from-the-Sun sky maximum and its rapid fade; Horvath et al., Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B / PMC5367315 for the sky-polarimetric navigation tests.
framing_note: MECHANISM plus the single best invitation rung in the sub-strand (Haidinger's brush -- a sense the reader has and has never been told about). ACCURACY RAIL 1: polarized sunglasses cut glare from horizontal NON-METALLIC surfaces near Brewster's angle -- do not overclaim them as blocking all reflections. RAIL 2: the sunstone rung must state the evidence honestly -- the recovered calcite is from a 1592 English warship, not a Viking ship, and no Viking-age sunstone has ever been found; the physics works, the archaeology does not close it. Never let a distractor secretly be the truth on this one. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: Haidinger's brush, then the LCD-goes-black-in-sunglasses rung. DISTRACTOR MINE: 'polarized lenses are just darker tint', 'polarizing is a kind of colour filter', birefringence confused with polarization, and the ether's transverse-wave embarrassment (a real historical consequence). TEACH-BEFORE-TEST: define 'polarized' concretely (one wobble direction) before any rung tests it.
history_overlap: ANIMAL bank owns honeybee navigation and the waggle dance as behaviour -- key the von Frisch rung to the SKY's polarization pattern being a usable compass, not to bee biology. HISTORY/GEOGRAPHY own Viking voyages -- key the sunstone rung only to the state of the physical evidence. The Rayleigh ladder in this sub-strand mentions sky polarization in one clause; keep the full treatment here.

name: Fluorescence: light that comes back changed
scope: Things that swallow light you cannot see and hand back light you can. T2: 1852, Cambridge -- George Gabriel Stokes passes sunlight through blue-violet glass onto a glass of quinine solution and watches an eerie blue glow appear in a thin layer right at the surface where the beam enters. He publishes it as 'On the Change of Refrangibility of Light' and names the effect FLUORESCENCE, after the mineral fluorspar that does the same thing. T3 (mechanism, teach the term): Stokes's rule -- what comes out is always LONGER in wavelength, lower in energy per photon, than what went in. The molecule absorbs a photon, quietly sheds a little of the energy as vibration, and re-emits the rest. You never get more energy per photon out than you put in, which is why an ultraviolet lamp can make things glow visibly but a red lamp cannot make them glow blue. T3 (invitation): tonic water under a blacklight glows electric blue, because of the quinine in it; highlighter ink glows; and laundry detergent leaves optical brighteners on white shirts, which is precisely why a white shirt blazes unnaturally under a club blacklight and why paper is sold as 'whiter than white'. Banknotes carry fluorescent security marks you can find in five minutes. T4 (corrected misconception): fluorescence stops within nanoseconds of the light going off; glow-in-the-dark stars keep going for hours because their excited state leaks slowly -- that is PHOSPHORESCENCE, a different clock, and the toys are not 'storing light' in any everyday sense. Modern ones use strontium aluminate; the radium-dial era is over and its story is a warning. T4: the fluorescent tube and the white LED are the same trick twice -- a tube makes ultraviolet from mercury vapour and a phosphor coating converts it to visible light, while a white LED is a blue LED under a yellow phosphor. Look at either through a CD and you see the phosphor's lumpy, banded output instead of a smooth rainbow. T5: the laboratory payoff -- Osamu Shimomura spent decades collecting jellyfish off Washington state and isolated green fluorescent protein; splicing its gene next to another gene makes a living cell LABEL its own protein in glowing green, turning invisible cell biology into something you can film. Nobel Prize 2008 with Martin Chalfie and Roger Tsien. T4: mineral fluorescence is a museum you can visit -- willemite glows green and calcite red under a blacklight, and the effect comes from trace impurity ions, not from the bulk mineral; prospectors used it to spot ore. T5 (MYSTERY): scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light and nobody knows why. Proposals include a by-product of cuticle hardening, a sunscreen, or a whole-body light detector -- genuinely unresolved, and the bank says so rather than picking one.
source: Grokipedia (Fluorescence; Photoluminescence; Stokes shift; Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet; Fluorescent lamp; Luminous paint; Blacklight) checked first via site search -- the 1852 paper 'On the Change of Refrangibility of Light', quinine and fluorspar, the naming, the Stokes shift and its vibrational-relaxation explanation; corroborated with Wikipedia 'Fluorescence' and 'Phosphorescence' (nanosecond vs long-lived emission, strontium aluminate in modern glow pigments), Wikipedia 'Green fluorescent protein' and the 2008 Nobel Prize in Chemistry citation (Shimomura, Chalfie, Tsien), Wikipedia 'Fluorescence' / Franklin, New Jersey mineral fluorescence for willemite and calcite.
framing_note: MECHANISM with an unusually high dinner-test density -- almost every rung is a five-minute experiment with a cheap UV torch. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: the tonic-water rung. ACCURACY RAIL 1: fluorescence is nanoseconds, phosphorescence is seconds to hours -- and never describe fluorescent objects as 'storing' light; the storing language belongs (loosely) to phosphorescence only. RAIL 2: the scorpion rung must stay OPEN -- state the competing proposals and that none is established; no distractor may quietly be the real answer. DISTRACTOR MINE: this topic has the best adjacent-but-wrong set in the sub-strand -- phosphorescence, chemiluminescence (a glow stick, where the energy comes from a chemical reaction and no light goes in), bioluminescence (a firefly, also chemical), and incandescence (a glowing filament, energy from heat). Four real, distinct mechanisms a reader will happily confuse. TEACH-BEFORE-TEST: define 'photon energy' and 'ultraviolet' before the Stokes-rule rung leans on them.
history_overlap: ANIMAL bank owns bioluminescent creatures and the jellyfish itself -- key GFP to the laboratory TOOL and the gene tag, and key the scorpion rung to the open question rather than to scorpion biology. A science CHEMISTRY sub-strand may own glow sticks -- use them only as a one-clause contrast.

name: How three cones fool you into seeing every colour
scope: Colour is manufactured, and there is an experiment for every claim in that sentence. T2: your eye contains only THREE colour sensors, and they are badly named -- the so-called 'red' cone actually peaks in the greenish-yellow around 560-580 nm and overlaps its neighbour heavily. Every colour any human has ever seen is three numbers. T2 (invitation): which is why a screen can lie to you. A television contains no yellow light at all; it makes yellow by firing red and green pixels so that your cones receive the same ratio real yellow light would produce. Two physically different spectra that look identical are METAMERS -- put a drop of water on a phone screen showing a yellow image and you will see the red and green dots. T3: 17 May 1861, Royal Institution -- James Clerk Maxwell has the photographer Thomas Sutton shoot a tartan ribbon three times through red, green and blue liquid filters, then projects the three positives back through the same three filters, superimposed. The world's first durable colour photograph is the cone theory built out of glass and lamps. T4 (payoff, REVERSAL): it should not have worked. Collodion plates were essentially BLIND to red, so Maxwell's red-filtered exposure had no business recording anything. In 1961 Ralph Evans found the answer -- the red dyes in the ribbon also reflect ULTRAVIOLET, which Sutton's red filter happened to pass and the plate could see. A century-old triumph turned out to be luck, and it took a hundred years for anyone to check. T3: Thomas Young proposed three receptors in 1802 for a hard-nosed reason -- the eye cannot plausibly carry a separate nerve for every wavelength -- and Helmholtz developed it. But Ewald Hering objected in 1872: you can easily imagine reddish blue and greenish yellow, yet nobody has ever seen a reddish GREEN or a bluish YELLOW, and three independent sensors do not explain that. T4: both men were right at different stages. Three cone types sit in the retina, and then the retina's own ganglion cells immediately re-encode them into OPPOSING channels -- red against green, blue against yellow, light against dark. Which is why afterimages come out in the opposite colour: stare at a red square for thirty seconds, look at a white wall, and cyan appears. T4: John Dalton published the first scientific account of colour blindness in 1794 from his own case, convinced the fluid in his eyeball was tinted blue, and asked that his eyes be examined after his death to test it. They were, in 1844: no blue tint at all. In 1995 DNA from his preserved eye showed he was a deuteranope, missing the green-cone pigment gene. His hypothesis was wrong, his self-report was gold, and he set up the test that refuted him. T5: red-green colour blindness runs far more common in men, roughly 8 percent against under 1 percent, because the green and red pigment genes sit side by side on the X chromosome and swap segments easily. And a small number of women carrying a variant pigment gene may be genuine TETRACHROMATS with a fourth working cone type -- a real claim with only a handful of confirmed cases, and still contested. T5: colour is not out there in the world. A wavelength is physical; the sensation is built. The dress that split the internet in 2015 is the cleanest demonstration ever run at scale -- identical pixels read as white-and-gold or blue-and-black depending on what your visual system ASSUMES about the light in the room, and it produced real published research. T5: more sensors is not more colour -- mantis shrimp carry twelve or more photoreceptor types and yet DISCRIMINATE between similar colours worse than humans do, which overturned a decade of popular claims about their vision.

framing_note: The perception flagship, and the sub-strand's best 'you are the easiest person to fool' ladder -- Maxwell fooled by his own lucky photograph, Dalton fooled by his own eyeball theory, everyone fooled by a dress. ACCURACY RAIL 1: the L cone peaks in yellow-green, not red -- say it correctly, since the misnaming IS a rung. RAIL 2: the 'first colour photograph' claim must carry the Evans 1961 correction; never present Maxwell's demonstration as a straightforwardly successful red-green-blue capture. RAIL 3: functional tetrachromacy in some women is a genuinely contested finding with few confirmed cases -- present it as contested, not as established. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: the water-drop-on-a-screen rung and the thirty-second afterimage, both doable while reading. DISTRACTOR MINE: 'the eye has one receptor per colour', Newton's seven colours treated as physical categories, Dalton's tinted-humour theory, Goethe's boundary theory, and 'screens make yellow using yellow light'. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: never state that three cones exist in a stem that asks what Young inferred; describe the problem he faced (a nerve per wavelength is impossible) and let the answer be recalled.
history_overlap: ANIMAL bank owns mantis shrimp and animal vision generally -- key that rung to the human comparison and the corrected popular claim, never to shrimp anatomy. A science BRAIN/perception sub-strand, if one exists, may claim #TheDress -- key it here to colour constancy as a light-and-colour mechanism. The Newton ladder in this sub-strand owns the seven-colours choice; reference only.

name: Soap bubbles, oil slicks and Newton's rings
scope: Colour with no pigment in it at all. T2: a soap bubble contains nothing coloured. The colours come from the film's THICKNESS -- light reflecting from the outer surface and light reflecting from the inner surface, a few hundred nanometres later, either reinforce or cancel each other, and which colour cancels depends on how thick the film is at that exact spot. Blow one and watch the bands drift downward as the film drains. T2 (invitation): which is why a bubble goes BLACK at the top just before it bursts -- as the film thins to well under a hundred nanometres, every visible wavelength cancels at once and the crown of the bubble turns transparent-dark. That black patch is a five-second warning that it is about to pop. T3: Newton's rings -- press a curved lens onto a flat glass plate and concentric coloured rings appear in the wedge of AIR trapped between them. Newton measured them with extraordinary care, tabulated the thicknesses, and then read them as evidence for particles undergoing 'fits of easy reflection'. He collected the best wave evidence of the century and interpreted it the other way. T3: Robert Hooke had already described these colours in thin mica sheets and soap films in Micrographia (1665) and guessed they were wave-like -- and the priority quarrel over them fed the long Hooke-Newton feud. T4: Thomas Young supplied the correct reading around 1802 -- interference -- along with one subtlety that seals it: light reflecting off a denser medium flips phase by half a wavelength, which is exactly why the very CENTRE of Newton's rings, where the air gap is zero and everything should reinforce, comes out DARK. That dark centre is the fingerprint of the flip. T4: engineers now do it on purpose -- the faint purple sheen on camera lenses and spectacles is an anti-reflection coating deliberately made a quarter-wavelength thick so the two reflections cancel; and a rainbow slick of oil on a wet road is a thickness MAP of the oil layer, thickest where the colours are dullest. T5: where this mechanism stops and another begins -- a bubble's colour comes from ONE film, but a butterfly's blue comes from many stacked layers, and an opal's flash from a lattice of packed silica spheres. Those structural colours never fade the way pigments do. And a CD or DVD splits light by DIFFRACTION off its track spacing, which is a genuinely different mechanism -- do not conflate the disc with the bubble.
source: Grokipedia (Thin-film interference; Soap film; Soap bubble; Newton's rings; Structural coloration; Cloud iridescence) checked first via site search -- Hooke's Micrographia (1665) thin-plate colours, Newton's systematic measurement and his 'fits' interpretation, Young's 1802 interference explanation of soap-film colours and the wedge-of-air geometry of Newton's rings; corroborated with Wikipedia 'Thin-film interference' (half-wave phase shift on reflection from a denser medium, the dark centre of Newton's rings, quarter-wave anti-reflection coatings) and Wikipedia 'Structural coloration' (multilayer reflectors, opal's sphere lattice) and 'Diffraction grating' (CD/DVD track spacing).
framing_note: MECHANISM, entirely kid-checkable with dish soap, a puddle and a pair of glasses. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: the black patch at the top of a bubble as a countdown to the pop. ACCURACY RAIL 1: the black film is destructive interference at sub-100 nm thickness, NOT 'the soap running out of colour' or the film becoming a mirror. RAIL 2: the dark centre of Newton's rings is the half-wave phase flip -- get this right or the rung is worthless. RAIL 3: CD and DVD colours are diffraction off track spacing, a different mechanism from thin films -- one rung must say so explicitly, and no other rung may blur them. DISTRACTOR MINE: 'the soap film is dyed', 'the bubble reflects the rainbow around it', Newton's own fits-of-easy-reflection theory (a live position held by the greatest physicist alive), diffraction offered where interference belongs, and Rayleigh scattering offered for the oil slick. name: The green flash at sunset
scope: A mini gem: a sight sailors reported for centuries and scientists dismissed as an eye trick. T3: in the last second or two before the Sun's upper edge disappears into a clean sea horizon, the top sliver can flare vivid GREEN. The atmosphere is acting as a weak prism -- it bends short wavelengths slightly more than long ones, so the Sun's blue-green image sets a fraction of a second later than its red image, and for an instant only the green edge is left. T4: for a long time the standard explanation was that it is not out there at all -- that a viewer staring at a red Sun gets a green AFTERIMAGE on the retina, exactly the opponent-process effect that makes a red square leave a cyan ghost. That was a serious hypothesis by serious people, and a photograph settles it: the French astronomer Lucien Rudaux published a photograph of the flash in 1925, and modern cameras record it routinely. Instruments do not have retinal fatigue. T4/T5: why it is rare even though the physics always happens -- the pure refractive effect is far too thin to see, so the flash needs a temperature inversion or a mirage layer over the water to magnify the separation, which is why a stable sea horizon or a high desert horizon gives the best odds, and why the blue that is bent even more is usually scattered away before it reaches you (which is also why 'blue flashes' are much rarer than green). It is genuinely checkable: clear horizon, no cloud bank, and do not stare at the Sun until it is nearly gone.
source: Grokipedia (Green flash; Atmospheric refraction; Mirage of astronomical objects; Atmospheric optics) checked first via site search -- differential refraction of the upper limb, the early dismissal as a physiological afterimage, Lucien Rudaux's first published photograph in 1925, and the role of mirage/inversion layers in magnifying the effect; corroborated with Wikipedia 'Green flash' (the inferior-mirage and mock-mirage flash types, the scattering of blue, and D.J.K. O'Connell's 1958 Vatican Observatory photographic study 'The Green Flash and Other Low Sun Phenomena').
framing_note: A small REVERSAL-plus-invitation ladder: a real phenomenon written off as an illusion of the observer until a camera settled it. Keep it to three rungs; it is a gem, not a keystone. ACCURACY RAIL: the afterimage hypothesis was reasonable, not stupid -- present it respectfully, and let the PHOTOGRAPH (Rudaux 1925; O'Connell's 1958 colour study, whose details should be confirmed at build time) be what decides it. Do not claim the flash is common or guaranteed; the honest version is that it needs an inversion or mirage layer and a clean horizon. Add a plain do-not-stare-at-the-Sun line. DISTRACTOR MINE: retinal afterimage (the real historical rival), Rayleigh scattering offered as the cause, a green ray from the Sun's own spectrum, and cloud refraction. DINNER-TEST PAYOFF: T3 -- the reader can go look for it on the next clear evening at a beach.
history_overlap: The colour-vision ladder in this sub-strand owns the opponent-process afterimage -- reference it in the T4 rung, do not re-teach it. GEOGRAPHY may own coastal or desert horizons place-first; key this ladder to the refraction mechanism only.
